result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): A's headline 'Pool open — OK to swim' answers both parts of the parents' question, and its large dark-on-white numbers with clear range text and a prominent 'Last tested: 14:05' read well from a distance. B's headline says only 'Pool is open' and leaves 'OK to swim' to a smaller subline; its range text and test time are smaller and lower in contrast on the dark background. Both are accurate, add no invented data and fit on one screen; A's range bars only show the supplied ranges. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): B's headline, 'Pool open – OK to swim', answers both halves of the parents' question. Its readings use larger numerals in high-contrast dark-on-light text, and its last-tested time stands out. The range bars B adds use only the supplied data and stay simple. A is clean and accurate, but its headline only says 'open', and its range text and last-tested time are small and lower-contrast on the dark background, so they're harder to read from a few metres away.
